{{short description|Form of DRM}}
{{use dmy dates|date=August 2020}}
'''Always-on DRM''' or '''always-online DRM''' is a form of [[digital rights management]] (DRM) that requires a [[consumer]] to remain connected to a [[Server (computing)|server]], especially through an [[internet connection]], to use a particular product. The practice is also referred to as '''persistent online authentication'''. The technique is meant to prevent [[Online piracy|copyright infringement of software]]. Like other DRM methods, always-on DRM has proven controversial, mainly because it has failed to stop pirates from illegally using the product, while causing severe inconvenience to people who bought the product legally due to the [[single point of failure]] it inherently introduces.

==Usage and criticism==
{{cleanup rewrite|2=section|date=August 2026|talk=Rewrite}}
Popular [[video game]]s such as ''[[Diablo III]]'', ''[[Super Mario Run]]'', and ''[[Starcraft 2]]'' employ always-on DRM by requiring players to connect to the internet to play, even in [[Single-player video game|single-player]] mode. Reviews of ''Diablo III'' criticized its use of always-on DRM.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pcadvisor.co.uk/news/game/3358011/diablo-iii-players-angry-as-hell-at-launch-chaos/ |title=Diablo III players angry as Hell at launch chaos |last=Jary |first=Simon |work=[[PC Advisor]] |date=16 May 2012 |accessdate=5 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102191108/http://www.pcadvisor.co.uk/news/game/3358011/diablo-iii-players-angry-as-hell-at-launch-chaos/|archive-date=2 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> As with ''Diablo III'', ''[[SimCity (2013 video game)|SimCity]]'' (2013) experienced bugs at its launch due to always-on DRM.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cinemablend.com/games/SimCity-Now-Available-Always-DRM-Causes-Major-Launch-Day-Issues-53303.html |title=SimCity Now Available; Always-On DRM Causes Major Launch Day Issues |last=Usher |first=William |work=Cinema Blend |date=5 March 2013 |accessdate=5 March 2013}}</ref> Its developer, [[Maxis]], initially defended the practice as being a result of the game's reliance on [[cloud computing]] for in-game processing, but it was later confirmed that cloud computing was only necessary to support the inter-city and social media mechanisms.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gamespot.com/news/maxis-simcitys-always-on-drm-for-gamers-benefit-6401896 |title=Maxis: SimCity's always-on DRM for gamers' benefit |last=Makuch |first=Eddie |date=21 December 2012 |publisher=[[GameSpot]] |accessdate=5 March 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=SimCity Boss's "Straight Answers" Seem Pretty Wiggly|url=http://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2013/03/16/simcity-bosss-straight-answers-seem-pretty-wiggly/|journal=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]|date=16 March 2013|accessdate=March 16, 2013|last1=Walker|first1=John}}</ref>  Tim Willits at [[id Software]] has also defended the use of always-on DRM, arguing that it would make [[Patch (computing)|updates]] easier. This later received even more criticism, with users stating that these updates could potentially render the game unable to be played.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-08-10-id-software-on-always-on-internet-debate |title=Id Software on always-on internet debate |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=10 August 2011 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]] |accessdate=5 March 2013}}</ref>

A major disadvantage of always-on DRM is that whenever the DRM authentication server goes down or a region experiences an Internet outage, it effectively locks out people from playing the game, hence the criticism.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.escapistmagazine.com/news/view/98927-Ubisoft-DRM-Authentication-Servers-Go-Down | title=Ubisoft DRM Authentication Servers Go Down | publisher=Escape Magazine | date=7 March 2010 | accessdate=26 January 2015}}</ref> Another major disadvantage is that when the servers for the game are shut down, the game is rendered completely unplayable without illegal DRM circumvention, such as in the case of ''[[Darkspore]]''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://techraptor.net/content/ea-shuts-down-darkspore-servers |title=Darkspore Servers Shut Down |last=Richard |first=Mark |date=2016-03-06 |website=techraptor.net |language=en-US |access-date=2018-05-20}}</ref> and the Mac edition of ''[[The Settlers 7]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://support.ubi.com/en-GB/Faqs/000023985/The-Settlers-7-Paths-to-a-Kingdom-on-Mac-will-be-discontinued-on-Date |title=The Settlers 7: Paths to a Kingdom on Mac will be discontinued on 06/10/2015 |website=Ubisoft |language=en-gb |access-date=2018-05-20}}</ref>

[[Ubisoft]]'s first titles requiring an always-on connection were ''[[Silent Hunter 5: Battle of the Atlantic]] and [[Assassin's Creed II]]'', of which the former had reportedly been cracked as of the first day of the game's release.<ref>Geek.com. [http://www.geek.com/articles/games/ubisofts-always-connected-games-drm-already-cracked-2010034/ Ubisoft’s always-connected games DRM already cracked] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111211023901/http://www.geek.com/articles/games/ubisofts-always-connected-games-drm-already-cracked-2010034 |date=11 December 2011 }}. Accessed 2013-03-12.</ref> ''[[Assassin's Creed II]]'' was later cracked on the day of its release in Japan.  Ubisoft also used always-on DRM in  ''[[Driver: San Francisco]]'', which was also cracked.<ref name=ign20120905>{{cite web |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2012/09/05/ubisoft-officially-ditches-always-on-pc-drm |title=Ubisoft Officially Ditches Always-On PC DRM |last=Karmali |first=Luke |date=5 September 2012 |publisher=[[IGN]] |accessdate=5 March 2013}}</ref> However, the company announced in September 2012 that it would not employ always-on DRM in its future games,<ref name=ign20120905/> although they decided to re-implement the DRM again for ''[[The Crew (video game)|The Crew]]'' (despite having a story mode), ''[[Tom Clancy's The Division|The Division]]'' (although it was never meant for single-player gameplay) and ''[[For Honor]]''. ''[[Assassin's Creed Odyssey]]'' also received backlash for being unavailable in offline mode in February 2019, to which Ubisoft has clarified that the always-online mode was a glitch that was to be fixed soon enough, although many other players did not face this issue and were able to play the game without an internet connection.

''The Crew'' garnered criticism due to it being always-online in spite of having a single-player campaign. Ubisoft later confirmed that the game would not be available offline, as they wanted to make the game a living world with multiplayer and single-player combined. In April 2024, the servers for ''The Crew'' were shut down, rendering the game unplayable.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Nightingale |first=Ed |date=2023-12-15 |title=Ubisoft delists The Crew, with servers shutting next year |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/ubisoft-delists-the-crew-with-servers-shutting-next-year |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en}}</ref> This caused severe player backlash, with multiple lawsuits as well as the [[Stop Killing Games]] consumer movement being launched.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carpenter |first=Nicole |date=2024-11-11 |title=Ubisoft sued for shutting down The Crew |url=https://www.polygon.com/gaming/476979/ubisoft-the-crew-shut-down-lawsuit-class-action/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=Polygon |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilde |first=Tyler |date=2024-04-05 |title=Gamers seek legal win that would stop developers from rendering online games unplayable: 'It is an assault on both consumer rights and preservation of media' |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/gaming-industry/stop-killing-games-campaign/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref> Due to the negative reactions, Ubisoft promised to bring an offline mode to ''[[The Crew 2]]'' and ''[[The Crew Motorfest]]'', sequels to ''The Crew'' that were also always-online at launch.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=2024-09-10 |title=After eating it for killing The Crew, Ubisoft promises to bring offline support to The Crew 2 and The Crew Motorfest |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/racing/after-eating-it-for-killing-the-crew-ubisoft-promises-to-bring-offline-support-to-the-crew-2-and-the-crew-motorfest/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dinsdale |first=Ryan |date=2024-09-12 |title=Ubisoft Adding Offline Modes to The Crew 2 and The Crew Motorfest, But the Original Is Gone for Good |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/ubisoft-adding-offline-modes-to-the-crew-2-and-the-crew-motorfest-but-the-original-is-gone-for-good |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref> ''The Crew 2'' received an offline mode in an October 2025 update, with ''Motorfest''{{'s}} implementation coming later.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Warren |first=Mark |date=2025-10-17 |title=The Crew 2's offline mode is live, so you don't have to worry as much about Ubisoft ramming it off the road |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/the-crew-2s-offline-mode-is-live-so-you-dont-have-to-worry-as-much-about-ubisoft-ramming-it-off-the-road |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=Rock, Paper, Shotgun |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chalk |first=Andy |date=2025-10-16 |title=Gamers hand Ubisoft a rare 'W' as The Crew 2's offline mode finally goes live |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/games/racing/gamers-hand-ubisoft-a-rare-w-as-the-crew-2s-offline-mode-finally-goes-live/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref>

[[Electronic Arts]] was later criticized for making their game ''[[Need for Speed (2015 video game)|Need for Speed]]'' (2015) always online, even though it had both single player and multiplayer modes. EA later stated that this was because the game was an ever-expanding world that would be constantly updated and that it would be required for taking snapshots and posting them on Autolog, which would earn the player Experience points and other rewards if the snapshots are liked enough.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Prescott |first=Shaun |date=2015-08-09 |title=Need For Speed will require an internet connection, and here's why |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/need-for-speed-will-require-an-internet-connection-and-heres-why/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref> This later garnered more criticism. In the end, it was later found out that the reason for drastic framerate drops in Need for Speed on all platforms was because of the always-online connection. Because of this, EA decided to make all their later games to be playable offline, with the next Need for Speed game, ''[[Need for Speed Payback|Payback]]'', having an offline single-player campaign mode.

[[Sony Interactive Entertainment]] and [[Polyphony Digital]] were later criticized for making their latest title, ''[[Gran Turismo 7]]'', require constant internet connection in order for players to be able to save their progress. The series creator [[Kazunori Yamauchi]] explains that this decision was made to prevent hacking and cheating, with only Arcade Mode being fully playable offline.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Square|first=Push|date=2022-02-02|title=Gran Turismo 7 Will Require an Online Connection on PS5, PS4 to Prevent Cheating|url=https://www.pushsquare.com/news/2022/02/gran-turismo-7-will-require-an-online-connection-on-ps5-ps4-to-prevent-cheating|access-date=2022-02-04|website=Push Square|language=en-GB}}</ref> This was met with severe criticism by reviewers, who noted the game's overall grind to earn credits and the online requirement being used as a major push for the game's microtransactions, More than a week after release, the game had a maintenance period during which it was unplayable for more than a day before being patched.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/22984748/gran-turismo-7-maintenance-downtime-credits-car-prices|title=Gran Turismo 7, offline for more than 24 hours, shows its always-online problem|website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|date=18 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/server-outage-hoiwthe-always-online-requirement-for-gran-turismo-7-jeopardizes-a-great-game/|title = The Always-Online Requirement for 'Gran Turismo 7' Jeopardizes a Great Game| date=18 March 2022 }}</ref>

[[Activision]] has recently been criticized for making their games on the PC always-online via [[Battle.net]] even if they have single-player modes. This was most apparent with ''[[Call of Duty: Modern Warfare (2019 video game)|Call of Duty Modern Warfare]]'' (2019),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dsogaming.com/news/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-is-always-online-on-the-pc-even-for-its-single-player-campaign/|title = Call of Duty: Modern Warfare is always-online on the PC, even for its single-player campaign|date = 25 October 2019}}</ref> ''[[Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2#Remastered|Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2 Remastered]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefpsreview.com/2020/04/01/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-2-campaign-remastered-doesnt-have-multiplayer-but-its-always-online-anyway/|title = Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Remaster Doesn't Have Multiplayer, but It's Always Online Anyway|date = 2 April 2020}}</ref> ''[[Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1+2]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epicgames.com/store/en-US/product/tony-hawks-pro-skater-1-and-2/home|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200911023438/https://www.epicgames.com/store/en-US/product/tony-hawks-pro-skater-1-and-2/home|archive-date=11 September 2020|title=Tony Hawk's™ Pro Skater™ 1 + 2 &#124; Download and Buy Today|date=4 September 2020 }}</ref> and ''[[Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://screenrant.com/crash-bandicoot-4-pc-version-always-online/|title=Crash Bandicoot 4's PC Version Requires an Internet Connection|website=[[Screen Rant]]|date=26 March 2021}}</ref>

''[[Hitman (2016 video game)|Hitman]]'' (2016) was later criticized to be always-online to be able to save in certain areas of levels in the game. [[Square Enix]] clarified that there would be no fix for it as the game was "a constantly, evolving, living world of assassination that will grow alongside the community with frequent content updates in between the launch of each location. This live content includes new contracts, escalation contracts, elusive targets, and even additional challenges", and while it is possible to play the game offline, two separate save states for both offline and online have been made.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dransfield |first=Ian |date=2016-03-25 |title=Hitman's online/offline save incompatibility won't be fixed |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/hitmans-onlineoffline-save-incompatibility-wont-be-fixed/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref> However, the game was later patched to make sure that all locations and levels could be fully played in offline mode, with the disadvantage being that leaderboards would not be accessible, regular updates would not be installed, live events would not be available for playing, and some areas could not be used as a starting point during missions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=2016-11-28 |title=Huge Hitman update makes unlocks work offline |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/hitman-update-makes-unlocks-work-offline |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=Eurogamer.net |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McKeand |first=Kirk |date=2016-11-28 |title=Hitman's 1.7.0 patch lets Agent 47 access his arsenal without an internet connection |url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/hitman/hitman-170-patch |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=PCGamesN |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Square Enix]] later received criticism for implementing always-on DRM on the [[Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster|remastered version of ''Final Fantasy X/X-2'']] in 2019, over two years after the game launched.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Square Enix Adds Always-Online DRM Requirement to Final Fantasy X and X-2 3 Years After Launch|url=https://www.game-debate.com/news/26819/square-enix-adds-always-online-drm-requirement-to-final-fantasy-x-and-x-2-3-years-after-launch|access-date=2020-06-14|website=Game-Debate}}</ref> Square Enix later removed the update altogether for further modifications.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-03-27|title=Steam :: FINAL FANTASY X/X-2 HD Remaster :: March 27th Update|url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/359870/announcements/detail/1717468247152498700|access-date=2020-06-14|website=steamcommunity.com|language=en}}</ref>

''[[Quantum Break]]'', a game developed by [[Remedy Entertainment|Remedy]] was also criticized for being always-online on the PC version, due to the fact that live episodes limited to 4K resolution had to be streamed because of storage limitations according to [[Microsoft]], despite the fact that personal computers can be constantly upgraded with more storage as time goes by. Nevertheless, it is possible to play the game offline without logging into Microsoft, but it will result in the live-action cutscenes in the game being disabled, leaderboards becoming inaccessible, and it will also result with another consequence, the game's protagonist Jack Joyce wearing a pirate [[eyepatch]], which is a reference to another Remedy-developed and Microsoft-published game ''[[Alan Wake]]'', where the protagonist Alan Wake would wear an eyepatch should the Steam version of the game ever be pirated. Playing the game offline without logging into [[Windows Store]] will make the game think that it has been pirated and make Jack wear the eyepatch, but warez group [[3DM]] managed to make a trainer for the game with an option to remove the eyepatch.

The 2016 [[reboot (fiction)|reboot]] of ''[[Doom (2016 video game)|Doom]]'' was also later criticized of requiring to be always-online in order to use the [[Vulkan (API)|Vulkan API]] recently implemented in the game in an update, although it can still run offline with the [[OpenGL]] executable.

Originally an online-only game, ''[[Star Wars Battlefront (2015 video game)|Star Wars: Battlefront]]'' (2015) was patched by Electronic Arts with an offline mode in July 2016.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Samuel |date=2016-07-20 |title=Star Wars Battlefront: offline mode, the Death Star, and Battlefront 2 |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/star-wars-battlefront-offline-mode-the-death-star-and-battlefront-2/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |work=PC Gamer |language=en}}</ref>

[[Xbox Play Anywhere]] games like ''[[ReCore]]'', ''[[Gears of War 4]]'', and ''[[Forza Horizon 3]]'' have also been criticized of being required to be online to be launched and to be authenticated every 24 hours. [[Denuvo]] was also immensely criticized of using a similar method, and many tech reviewers had problems benchmarking Denuvo-implemented games like ''[[Tom Clancy]]'s [[Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands|Ghost Recon: Wildlands]]'' and ''[[Deus Ex: Mankind Divided]]''.

As of October 2015, in the U.S. always-online games with single player modes that now have had dead servers for six months and longer are now exempt from [[DMCA]] prohibitions on circumventing copyright protection.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://copyright.gov/fedreg/2015/80fr65944.pdf|title = Exemption to Prohibition on Circumvention of Copyright Protection Systems for Access Control Technologies|date = October 28, 2015|accessdate = December 12, 2015|website = www.copyright.gov|publisher = |last = |first = }}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=July 2022}}

During the month of October 2019 with the launch of ''[[Rockstar Games#Rockstar Games Launcher|Rockstar Games Launcher]]'', the single player story mode for the game ''[[Grand Theft Auto V]]'' sold and distributed through ''[[Steam (service)|Steam]]'' required activation via the internet every time during the game startup process, whereas previously the game required periodic activation every few days. Whether this was intentional or defective by design due to the effect of implementing ''[[Rockstar Games#Rockstar Games Launcher|Rockstar Games Launcher]]'' as an extra layer of [[digital rights management|DRM]] for the game is unclear, neither the game developer and publisher ''[[Rockstar Games]]'', or the game distributor ''[[Valve Corporation|Valve]]'' has publicly acknowledged or commentated on the change in status of the [[digital rights management|DRM]]. On 5 November 2019 ''[[Rockstar Games]]'' rolled out an update to the ''[[Rockstar Games#Rockstar Games Launcher|Rockstar Games Launcher]]'' which reverted the [[digital rights management|DRM]] status of ''[[Grand Theft Auto V]]'' from Always-on DRM back to its previous periodic activation implementation.

Always-on DRM is not restricted to computer games, as it was discovered early into the [[ninth generation of video game consoles]] that a form of it exists in the programming and design of three generations of [[PlayStation]] consoles, the [[PlayStation 3]], the [[PlayStation 4]], and the [[PlayStation 5]], as well as the [[Xbox Series X/S]], due to gaming consoles' increasing reliance on internet connectivity.  All three PlayStation consoles can only be fully operational when persistently connected to the [[PlayStation Network]] and depend on it to maintain the date and time, which are used to prevent players from [[cheating in video games|cheating]] by claiming that they unlocked Trophies at an unreasonably early time.  When such connection is lost, these systems rely on an internal [[CMOS battery]] to maintain the date and time, and if that is depleted or removed, all digitally downloaded games become unplayable as the system would thus have no means to ascertain the current date and time.  This issue, known as [[C-bomb (PlayStation Network)|C-bomb]], adversely affects the PS4 most, as the mandatory date and time check also extends to physical games, meaning that such system will be unable to play any games at all should such check fail.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Orland |first1=Kyle |title=The looming software kill-switch lurking in aging PlayStation hardware |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2021/04/the-looming-software-kill-switch-lurking-in-aging-playstation-hardware/ |website=[[Ars Technica]] |access-date=31 August 2021 |date=15 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Koch |first1=Cameron |title=Aging Batteries Could Turn PS3s & PS4s Into Paperweights |url=https://screenrant.com/playstation-console-battery-lifespan-problem-ps3-ps4/ |website=ScreenRant |access-date=31 August 2021 |date=16 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=De Meo |first1=Francesco |title=PlayStation 5 Runs Only Select Physical Games and No Digital Game Offline With Missing CMOS Battery |url=https://wccftech.com/playstation-5-cmos-battery/ |website=WCCFTech |access-date=31 August 2021 |date=18 April 2021}}</ref>  In late September 2021, Sony released a [[firmware]] update for the PS4 that resolved the issue, so that only time-stamping of Trophies would be disabled if no accurate date and time can be obtained from PSN.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Oneto |first1=Petey |title=PS4 Firmware Update Reportedly Keeps Consoles From Being Bricked |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/ps4-clock-battery-bricking-consoles |website=IGN |access-date=25 September 2021 |date=24 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Wen |first1=Alan |title=PS4 CMOS battery issue reportedly fixed in firmware update |url=https://www.nme.com/en_asia/news/gaming-news/ps4-cmos-battery-issue-reportedly-fixed-in-firmware-update-3052786 |website=NME |access-date=25 September 2021 |date=22 September 2021}}</ref>  A similar fix was also issued for the PS5 in November.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Ali |title=PS5 issue that might have locked players out of digital games appears to have been fixed |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/ps5-issue-that-might-have-locked-players-out-of-digital-games-appears-to-have-been-fixed/ |website=GamesRadar |access-date=3 November 2021 |date=2 November 2021}}</ref>  The Xbox Series X/S has a DRM system that requires the console to remain connected to the [[Xbox network]] to set up the system or start disc-based [[backwards compatible]] games.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Billings |first1=Kevin James |title=Xbox Series X DRM Makes Certain Games Completely Unplayable Offline |url=https://gamerant.com/xbox-series-x-drm-makes-certain-games-completely-unplayable-offline/ |website=GameRant |access-date=31 August 2021 |date=25 May 2021}}</ref>  In September 2022, Microsoft issued a system update that allowed backwards compatibility to function offline.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Totilo |first1=Stephen |title=Microsoft eases DRM restriction on many Xbox games |url=https://www.axios.com/2022/09/22/microsoft-drm-restriction-xbox-games |website=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |access-date=10 October 2022 |date=22 September 2022}}</ref>  These DRM measures can hinder [[video game preservation]] should the online services that use them become discontinued at any point in the future.

== Circumvention ==
Always-on DRM can be circumvented mainly by the use of custom servers made by the game's community<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 October 2022 |title=How To Set Up Genshin Impact Private Server To Unlock All Characters And Weapons |url=https://www.talkesport.com/guides/how-to-set-up-genshin-impact-private-server-to-unlock-all-characters-and-weapons/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221100728/https://www.talkesport.com/guides/how-to-set-up-genshin-impact-private-server-to-unlock-all-characters-and-weapons/ |archive-date=21 December 2022 |access-date=21 January 2023}}</ref> via [[reverse engineering]] game clients and studying how they communicate with servers, then re-implementing those functions on a custom server. The success-rate of such efforts is contingent on several factors, such as how much of a game’s systems are processed on the server, whether the game’s official servers are still running, and how much interest the game-playing public has had in the game to begin with. Efforts to revive [[EA Phenomic]]’s [[BattleForge]] (which reached end-of-life in 2013<ref>{{cite web |url=http://forums.battleforge.com/forum/showthread.php?t=80261 |title=BattleForge News: Important: BattleForge is being retired |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130910060412/http://forums.battleforge.com/forum/showthread.php?t=80261 |archive-date=2013-09-10 }}</ref>) with a custom server bore fruit as early as 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gamestar.de/spiele/battleforge/news/battleforge_reborn,44416,3233541.html |title=BattleForge Reborn - Community will das Spiel wiederbeleben|website=Gamestar|date=14 July 2015|language=de|publisher=[[GameStar]] |access-date=2016-06-26|last1=Dietrich|first1=Mathias}}</ref> with full functionality to the game restored in 2021. Meanwhile, no such breakthroughs exist for [[Maxis Emeryville]]’s ''[[Darkspore]]'', which was sunset in early 2016<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pcgamer.com/darkspore-will-close-for-good-next-week/|title=Darkspore will close for good next week|first=Andy|last=Chalk|work=[[PC Gamer]]|date=February 24, 2016|access-date=February 24, 2016}}</ref> and remains unplayable as of 2024.
